unit-m33.title: Topic 3 · 3-3 Decimals to Thousandths
unit-m33.source: enVision Math, Topic 3 textbook scan — Lessons 3-1 to 3-7 (Drive)

summary.text: Lesson 3-3 pushes the place-value chart three seats right of the decimal point: reading and writing thousandths, converting between decimals and fractions over 1,000, and the same ×10-per-seat relationship running through the point.

why.text: Thousandths are where money and measurement intuition run out and the chart has to carry you. The two classic errors — 97/1,000 as 0.97, and the ×10 rule pointed the wrong way — both come from trusting digits over seats, and both are in the quiz.

objectives.text: Write a thousandths fraction as a decimal and back.
Name the seat of any digit through the thousandths place.
Compare the values of one digit in neighbouring seats, in the correct direction.

parentNote.text: Watch the 0.097-vs-0.97 error — it is the single most common slip in this lesson, and it comes from copying digits without counting places. If she gets the Owen question wrong, the direction of the ÷10 ladder is the thing to talk through.

nextUp.text: Cards first — the last card is the one that prevents the classic mistake. Then the quiz.

cards.def:
**One of 1,000 equal parts of a whole — written 0.001.**
• The thousandths place is the THIRD place right of the decimal point.
• 4/1,000 = 0.004.
cards.hint: Three zeros in 1,000 — three places right of the point.

cards.def:
**Right of the decimal point the seats are tenths, hundredths, thousandths.**
• Each seat right is worth one-tenth of the seat before.
• The same ×10 ladder as whole numbers, just descending.
cards.hint: Same ladder, going down: ÷10 every step right.

cards.def:
**A decimal in thousandths is a fraction with denominator 1,000.**
• 0.444 = 444/1,000.
• The number of decimal places matches the zeros in the denominator.
cards.hint: Places right of the point = zeros in the bottom of the fraction.

cards.def:
**Read the digits as a whole number, then say the last place's name.**
• 0.309 → "three hundred nine thousandths".
• 0.05 → "five hundredths".
cards.hint: The last seat names the whole thing.

cards.def:
**A zero between the point and the digits pushes everything one seat smaller.**
• 97/1,000 is 0.097 — NOT 0.97.
• Check by counting places: thousandths needs three.
cards.hint: Count places, never just copy digits over.

questions.hint: Count how many places right of the point the 7 sits.
steps: The 7 sits three places right of the decimal point.
Three places right is the thousandths seat.

ex.main: **7/1,000.** Third seat right of the point means thousandths.
ex.tip: Places right of the point and zeros in the denominator always agree.

questions.q: A beetle measures 391/1,000 of a metre. How is that written as a decimal?
questions.hint: Thousandths means three places right of the point.
steps: The denominator 1,000 says thousandths.
Thousandths means exactly three decimal places.
391 fills them: 0.391.

ex.main: **0.391 m.** Three digits, three places — a clean fit.
ex.tip: The unit rides along: 0.391 of a METRE. Keep units attached to answers.

questions.q: Which digit of 2.583 is in the thousandths place?
questions.hint: Count seats rightward from the point.
steps: First seat right of the point: 5 (tenths).
Second: 8 (hundredths).
Third: 3 (thousandths).

ex.main: **3.** Third seat right of the point.
ex.tip: The ones seat is three seats left of the thousandths seat — worth 1,000 times as much. Count seats; never guess the factor.

questions.q: How is "seven hundred five thousandths" written as a decimal?
questions.hint: The missing tens place still needs a digit.
steps: Seven hundred five = 705.
Thousandths means three decimal places.
705 fills them: 0.705 — the zero holds the hundredths seat.

ex.main: **0.705.** The silent place in "seven hundred five" becomes a written 0.
ex.tip: Words skip empty places; decimals never can.

questions.hint: One seat apart on the ladder.
steps: 0.04 has its 4 in the hundredths seat.
0.004 has its 4 in the thousandths seat — one seat further right.
One seat is one factor of 10, and leftward is greater.

ex.main: **0.04 is 10 times as great.** Same ×10-per-seat rule as whole numbers.
ex.tip: The ladder never changes — it just keeps going past the point.

questions.q: A relay team ran 0.3 of the race in the rain. How many thousandths is 0.3?
questions.hint: Annex zeros until you reach the thousandths seat.
steps: 0.3 = 0.300 — annexing zeros changes nothing.
0.300 read in thousandths is 300 of them.

ex.main: **300/1,000.** Three tenths and three hundred thousandths are the same amount.
ex.tip: Renaming into smaller pieces is the move that makes decimal addition line up later.

questions.q: Nadia says 97/1,000 can be written as 0.97. What should you tell her?
opts: Thousandths needs three places, so it is 0.097
questions.hint: Count the decimal places her version uses.
steps: 0.97 uses only two decimal places — that is 97 HUNDREDTHS.
The denominator 1,000 demands three places.
Pad the front: 097 → 0.097.

ex.main: **0.097.** Two places is hundredths; her digits are right but the seats are wrong.
ex.tip: The zero in front of the 9 is doing real work — it is not decoration.

questions.q: Owen claims that in 0.555, the 5 in the thousandths place is worth 10 times the 5 in the hundredths place. What is wrong with his claim?
opts: The two 5s are worth the same because the digits match
He has it backwards — the thousandths 5 is worth one-tenth as much
questions.hint: Which direction does the ladder grow?
steps: The thousandths seat is one seat RIGHT of the hundredths seat.
Each seat right is worth one-tenth as much, not ten times.
So the thousandths 5 (0.005) is a tenth of the hundredths 5 (0.05).

ex.main: **He has the direction backwards.** Rightward seats shrink; leftward seats grow.
ex.tip: The size of the factor (10) was right — the direction is the whole question.

questions.q: A number has a 6 in the tenths place. If that 6 moved one seat to the right, what would happen to its value?
opts: It would be worth one-tenth as much
It would be worth 10 times as much
It would keep the same value
It would be worth one-hundredth as much
questions.hint: Moving right goes down the ladder.
steps: In the tenths seat the 6 is worth 0.6.
One seat right is the hundredths seat: 0.06.
0.06 is one-tenth of 0.6.

ex.main: **One-tenth as much.** Every seat rightward divides by 10.
ex.tip: Same digit, same rule, either side of the point.

questions.hint: Three zeros below means three places — then place the 40.
steps: Thousandths means three decimal places.
040 fills them: 0.040.
Check: 0.040 = 0.04 = 4 hundredths = 40 thousandths. ✓

ex.main: **0.040.** Forty thousandths and four hundredths are the same number in two coats.
ex.tip: A trailing zero changes nothing; a LEADING zero after the point changes everything.
